captions.text: SLS: 98 m tall. Mobile Launcher: 116 m. Kennedy Space Center, Pad 39B.
Four RS-25 engines start, burning liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen.
The two solid boosters ignite. They supply over 75% of the 8.8 million pounds of liftoff thrust.
The rocket climbs clear. The mobile launcher stays on the ground.
Max-Q: the strongest aerodynamic load. The structure must withstand the pressure and vibration.
About two minutes after liftoff, the boosters run out of fuel. Time is compressed here.
The empty side boosters separate and drift away. The four core engines keep firing.
Crossing the Kármán line: 100 km, the conventional edge of space. Reaching orbit also needs sideways speed.
The escape tower could pull Orion away in an emergency. Now its motor carries it clear.
The core stage keeps accelerating the spacecraft. This climb takes several minutes in real flight.
Main engine cutoff: the core stage has finished its job.
The orange core separates. Orion remains attached to the upper stage.
Coasting above Earth. The upper stage waits for the right place to burn. Time is shortened here.
Later, the upper-stage engine raises the low part of the orbit.
Orbit! About 28,000 km/h in low Earth orbit. Next: our fictional Mars journey.
